1.pericope_label: The heaven is my throne, and the earth is my footstool
debates: What occasion prompted the saying about the temple
Whether a word has dropped from the second verse
What the contrite heart is set against
outliers: Ellicott rejects all three historical occasions usually proposed and reads the words as a general truth instead
themes: A building measured against the one who fills it
Reverence for a sanctuary compatible with denying it contains God
Sacrifice emptied by the offerer’s indifference
The contrite heart named as the true counterpart of holiness

3.pericope_label: He that killeth an ox is as if he slew a man
debates: Whether the verse compares two acts or identifies them
Whether the fault is formalism or the continuance of abolished sacrifice
Whether a word has been lost from the second clause
outliers: Clarke holds that most interpreters have lost the sense by departing from the literal rendering, since sacrifice and murder cannot really be of one account with God
themes: Apostasy possible beneath an unexceptionable ritual
Sacrifice continued past the time appointed for it
A choice answered by a corresponding choice
Delusion granted as the punishment of preferring it

5.pericope_label: Your brethren that hated you said, Let the LORD be glorified
debates: Whether the persecution described belongs to the return from captivity or to the first preaching of the gospel
Whether the fifth verse says your brethren said or say ye to your brethren
What the voice from the city announces
outliers: Clarke prefers a reading attested by the Syriac and one Greek edition that turns the clause from report into command
themes: Terror to the wicked distinguished from comfort to the righteous
Excommunication pronounced in the name of God
Ruins that keep the holiness conferred on them
A noise identified only in the third clause

7.pericope_label: Before she travailed, she brought forth
debates: Whether the man-child is the new Israel or a whole nation of men
Whether the birth described is the first preaching of the gospel or a later conversion
Whether the eighth verse opens its second question with a conjunction
outliers: Clarke gives the literal force of the birth term and advises that it be avoided in public prayer and preaching
themes: Deliverance so sudden it precedes its own labour
Slow national growth set against supernatural speed
A work God will not leave unfinished
Credit for the birth reserved to God rather than the church

10.pericope_label: Rejoice ye with Jerusalem; I will extend peace to her like a river
debates: Whether the eleventh verse states a purpose, a consequence or a reason
Whether a word in the eleventh verse is corrupt
Which period the promised peace belongs to
outliers: Clarke observes that two Jewish commentators effectively concede a corrupt text while denying they are doing so
themes: Onlookers invited to become nurslings
The nations friendly to Zion made citizens of her
Inward and outward blessing promised together
A textual doubt confessed under cover of a gloss

13.pericope_label: As one whom his mother comforteth, so will I comfort you
debates: Why the word man is used rather than son
What the bones stand for in the figure
Whether the comfort described is administered directly or through means
outliers: Keil and Delitzsch defend a word a critic called ill-chosen by taking the people, once thought of as children, as standing before the prophet as a single man
themes: Human tenderness treated as the shadow of a greater
A returning exile rather than an infant at the breast
The body pictured as a tree reviving
One hand known in mercy and in anger at once

15.pericope_label: The LORD will come with fire, and with his chariots like a whirlwind
debates: Whether God comes in fire or as fire
What the phrase rendered behind one tree denotes
Whether the judgment falls on the heathen only or on Israel as well
outliers: Clarke reports a proposal to read a feminine form naming a moon-goddess, and calls the arguments for it not improbable
themes: One passage dark on one side and bright on the other
Fire read as belonging to God before it touches the world
Weapons of the persecutor turned into instruments of judgment
A single obscure word carrying a whole account of idolatry

18.pericope_label: I will set a sign among them, and send those that escape to the nations
debates: What verb is missing at the head of the eighteenth verse
What the sign set among them is
Which nations the names in the nineteenth verse denote
outliers: Clarke suspects the phrase who draw the bow is a corrupted national name, the bow having been added to make sense of a misread word
themes: A sentence whose main verb has to be supplied
A remnant preserved in order to be sent
Heralds despatched to nations that never heard the report
Judgment made the turning-point of a wider mercy

20.pericope_label: They shall bring all your brethren for an offering unto the LORD
debates: Whether the priests taken are Gentiles or Israelites of other tribes
Whether the new heavens are the gospel age or a literal new creation
What the vehicles named in the twentieth verse were
outliers: Ellicott thinks the prophet was keeping the middle wall of partition standing, where Keil and Delitzsch have it coming down at this very point
themes: Returning exiles counted as the offering itself
A priesthood qualified by character rather than descent
Continuity kept through a new creation
Brotherhood defined by faith rather than nation

23.pericope_label: From one new moon to another shall all flesh come to worship
debates: Whether new moons and sabbaths are literally kept in the promised state
Whether the last verse describes punishment after death or destruction on earth
What the going forth of the worshippers means
outliers: Ellicott holds that the closing words, taken strictly, describe an earthly defeat, while conceding that they became the starting-point of a doctrine of the next world
themes: A book ending with blessing and condemnation together
Pilgrimage widened from a nation to all flesh
A valley of past idolatry lending its name to a doctrine
Suffering pictured by an image the prophet leaves transient
